key_insight: MELD-graph kept similar sensitivity for focal cortical dysplasia at 7T MRI, but specificity dropped versus 3T, even after 7T-specific pipeline adjustments.
clinical_relevance: 7T outputs may help support radiologist review in difficult epilepsy cases, but false positives mean results should be interpreted cautiously rather than used alone.
method: Paired 3T and 7T MRI from 23 patients with FCD and 39 healthy controls across four epilepsy centres were analyzed.
MELD-graph was tested on 3T, on 7T with the default pipeline, and on 7T with adaptations for bias correction, skull-stripping, and sub-millimetric reconstruction.
ComBat harmonisation was also evaluated, with and without FLAIR at 7T.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on paired multicentre data showed 65% sensitivity at 3T versus 48%-52% at 7T, while specificity fell from 76% at 3T to 39%-45% at 7T.
watch_item: The main implementation concern is a higher false-positive rate at 7T, especially in the basal temporal lobes, which could reduce clinical confidence if not carefully reviewed.
paper_title: Multi-centre validation of MELD-graph for automated focal cortical dysplasia detection using 7T compared to paired 3T MRI
